description: Session-note compliance rule set for 97151 (assessment), 97153 (direct care), and 97155 (BCBA supervision). Transcribed 2026-09-27 from live Brellium Question Studio screenshots (pasted directly by Krishna, not drafted from general ABA knowledge) — see docs/ for provenance. The transcription itself flags a real chance a few 97155 rows below the visible screenshot fold weren't captured; spot-check against the live Question Studio for completeness before treating this 97155 list as exhaustive. 97156 (family/caregiver guidance) is NOT covered by this rule set — no 97156 question list was transcribed; do not assume 97155's rules apply to it without confirming first.

check_type_legend.deterministic: Structural/arithmetic fact, zero cost/variance — see fields.py.
check_type_legend.judgment: Genuine reading-comprehension call — goes through judge.py's majority-vote FINDINGS_TOOL call. A rule with needs_history=true has its extra_context built by history_comparison.py from prior_extractions first (short-circuited straight to not_checkable, never reaching judge.py, when no prior_extractions were passed in) — see the needs_history field below.
check_type_legend.not_checkable: Needs a second data source that genuinely doesn't exist yet for this specific record (a prior session note, a prior Treatment Plan version) — marked by design, not guessed at. CORRECTED (this phase): the Activity Statement — this batch's own timesheet, already sitting in the same uploaded PDF — is NOT one of these anymore; every 'align with the timesheet'/'15-minute break' rule is deterministic now (see fields.py::_check_timesheet_alignment / _check_same_day_location_break). A rule should only land on not_checkable when the thing it needs is outside (a) this document itself and (b) the Activity Statement, and that outside thing genuinely isn't available yet — never because the pipeline forgot the Activity Statement exists.

needs_history_note: needs_history=true marks the copy-paste / identical-data-point rules — the ones history_comparison.py handles by building their extra_context from this person's prior_extractions before judge.py ever sees them.

rules.description: Are there no names other than the patient's legal name or AKA mentioned in the note?
rules.notes: Requires reading comprehension to detect any other proper name mentioned in narrative text.

rules.description: Do all service locations billed match the location on the notes?
rules.notes: Structural: compare the note's own 'Session Location:' field against the location printed in the same document (e.g. the cover page's service-row location column).

rules.description: Do all the narratives only include content relevant to ABA therapy?
rules.notes: Content-relevance judgment call — no reliable keyword/structural signal for off-topic narrative content.

rules.description: Do the notes' start time, end time, date of service and location align with the timesheet?
rules.notes: The timesheet IS the Activity Statement page already sitting in the same uploaded batch PDF (classify_batch.py's own cover-page marker) — see fields.py::_check_timesheet_alignment / activity_statement.py. Compares this document's own extracted start/end time, date, and location against the timesheet row matching its own appendix. not_checkable only when the batch genuinely has no Activity Statement data recorded for it, or no row references this appendix — never a standing 'no timesheet available' assumption.

rules.description: Does the session summary's account of who was present agree with the 'Participants' section, in both directions — is anyone mentioned in the narrative (peers, siblings, or other participants) also checked as present, AND is anyone checked as present (e.g. a peer) also actually described in the narrative?
rules.notes: DECIDED (real manual audit round, both directions confirmed as real violations worth flagging): a checked-present participant with ZERO narrative support is just as real a documentation gap as an unchecked narrative mention -- a reviewer/auditor checking whether the note actually substantiates everyone billed/logged as present needs both directions caught, not just one. Do NOT treat 'checked as present but never described in the narrative' as automatically fine just because the rule used to read one-directionally -- that pattern is now also a FAIL, same severity as the original direction. Requires detecting person-mentions in freeform narrative text and cross-referencing against the Participants checkboxes.

rules.description: If the service location was not telehealth, were telehealth platforms not mentioned?
rules.notes: Conditional keyword search: only runs when 'Session Location' != Telehealth; then checks narrative text for known telehealth-platform keywords (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.).

rules.description: If the Session Location is "99-other" is there an accompanying community statement?
rules.notes: Conditional presence check on the 'referred to as N/A'/community-statement field seen in real fixtures whenever location is '99-other place of service'.

rules.description: Is the session note devoid of reference to punishment, and school goals?
rules.notes: Keyword/phrase search for 'punishment' and school-goal language.

rules.description: Is the session summary sufficiently detailed given the length of the session (2 components per hour)?
rules.notes: What counts as a narrative 'component' is not a countable structural unit here (contrast with 97153/97155's own 'sentences per hour' phrasing, which IS countable) — genuine reading-comprehension judgment.

rules.description: Was a parent or caregiver present for at least one assessment session?
rules.notes: Structural: OR across this person's assessment documents' own 'Participants: Parent/Caregiver' checkbox field.

rules.description: Was goal development or goal updating mentioned in at least one session note?
rules.notes: RECLASSIFIED from judgment (Phase 2 follow-up round): real sample PDFs show this maps directly onto the Assessment Activities block's own 'Treatment plan development' checkbox — a literal, structural restatement of this rule's own question, not a fuzzy keyword proxy for something else. Unlike the other judgment rules reconsidered in this same pass (peer/sibling narrative mentions, BCBA-presence consistency), there's no real ambiguity to vote on here. See fields.py::_check_SN_97151_11. Same single-document 'at least one' scope limitation as SN-97151-10: a checked box in this document conclusively passes; its absence here resolves to not_checkable, not fail, since it can't rule out another of this person's assessment documents.

rules.description: Was the session note devoid of references to nap/sleep or sickness?
rules.notes: Keyword/phrase search for nap/sleep/sickness language.

rules.description: Was the total length of the assessment 8 hours or less (5 hours or less if this was a Healthfirst client)?
rules.notes: Arithmetic: sum this person's assessment-document session durations; threshold depends on the note's own printed Insurance field (Healthfirst -> 5h, else 8h).

rules.description: Were all of the narratives NOT copy and pasted from a previous session?
rules.notes: history_comparison.py builds this rule's extra_context from prior_extractions before it reaches judge.py — see api.py's review_person_document. When no prior_extractions were passed in, history_comparison.py short-circuits this rule straight to not_checkable, never sending it to judge.py at all.

rules.description: Were all of the notes signed within 1 day of the date of service?
rules.notes: Date math: signature date vs. Session Date.

rules.description: Were all session lengths under 2 hours?
rules.notes: Arithmetic on Session Duration/Session Units.

rules.description: Were any of the sessions not double billed with any other sessions?
rules.notes: Needs a full same-provider/same-client billing ledger to detect overlapping billed sessions elsewhere — not available to a single-document, stateless review call.

rules.description: Are no names other than the patient's legal name or AKA used?
rules.notes: Same reasoning as SN-97151-01.

rules.description: Are the data points NOT identical to a previous session?
rules.notes: See SN-97151-14's note on history_comparison.py.

rules.description: Are there at least 3 goals worked on per hour billed?
rules.notes: Structural: real 97153 fixtures show bullets shaped 'X added a data point N to <goal text> for MM/DD/YYYY.' — count distinct goal-text bullets / extract embedded dates from them. Count distinct goal-text bullets, divide by session hours, threshold >= 3.

rules.description: Do the note's start time, end time, date of service and location align with the timesheet?
rules.notes: The timesheet IS the Activity Statement page already sitting in the same uploaded batch PDF (classify_batch.py's own cover-page marker) — see fields.py::_check_timesheet_alignment / activity_statement.py. Compares this document's own extracted start/end time, date, and location against the timesheet row matching its own appendix. not_checkable only when the batch genuinely has no Activity Statement data recorded for it, or no row references this appendix — never a standing 'no timesheet available' assumption.

rules.description: Does the BCBA/LBA documented on the note match the BCBA/LBA at the signature?
rules.notes: String comparison of the 'BCBA/LBA:' header field against the signature block name. CONDITIONAL: only applies when SN-97153-21 ('Was this NOT a supervised session?') answers No (i.e. the session genuinely was supervised) — this refinement was already worked out earlier in this project.

rules.description: Does the session summary only mention content relevant to ABA Therapy?
rules.notes: Same reasoning as SN-97151-03.

rules.description: Does the session summary's account of who was present agree with the 'who attended session' section, in both directions — is anyone mentioned in the narrative (peers, siblings, or other participants) also checked as present, AND is anyone checked as present (e.g. a peer) also actually described in the narrative?
rules.notes: DECIDED (real manual audit round, both directions confirmed as real violations worth flagging — this exact rule_id is where the 3-way judge inconsistency was found and root-caused): a checked-present participant with ZERO narrative support (e.g. 'Peer' checked in the attendance section but the session summary never mentions a peer at all) is just as real a documentation gap as an unchecked narrative mention -- FAIL both directions, same severity. Do NOT treat 'checked as present but never described' as automatically fine just because the rule used to read one-directionally. Same reasoning as SN-97151-05 otherwise.

rules.description: If the Session Location is "99-other" is there an accompanying community statement?
rules.notes: Same reasoning as SN-97151-07.

rules.description: If two sessions occur on the same day with different locations, is there at least a 15-minute break between them?
rules.notes: Turns out NOT to need a sibling PersonDocument at all — the Activity Statement cover page already lists every billable row for this date (start/end time + location each) in one place. See fields.py::_check_same_day_location_break / activity_statement.py. not_applicable when there's only one billable session that day (nothing to compare); not_checkable only when no Activity Statement data is recorded for this batch at all.

rules.description: Is the BCBA's presence (or lack thereof) consistently documented?
rules.notes: Cross-references a structured checkbox field against how BCBA presence is (or isn't) described in freeform narrative — semantic consistency check. SHARPENED (real-run follow-up, 2026-09-28): a real run found this coin-flipping between two structurally-identical real 97153 documents (confident pass on one, a genuine 3-way pass/uncertain/fail split on the other), traced to inconsistent reading of standard signature-page attestation language. A BCBA co-sign/attestation statement on the signature page (e.g. 'I attest that I provided adequate supervision as required... I am fully involved in the case which includes the review of session notes rendered by the behavior technician') is a standard ADMINISTRATIVE co-sign — it is NOT itself a claim that the BCBA was present during the session, and must not be read as contradicting a 'No' answer to 'Was this session Supervised by the BCBA/LBA?' or an unchecked BCBA/LBA box in the attendance section. Only flag a real inconsistency when the SESSION NARRATIVE ITSELF (not the signature/attestation block) describes the BCBA as present or active DURING the session — e.g. the narrative says the BCBA observed, directed, or participated in the session in real time. A co-sign attesting to supervision oversight AFTER the fact is routine and expected on every note regardless of whether the BCBA attended that specific session, and is never itself grounds for a fail/uncertain here. If a real re-run still shows a genuine split on well-formed documents after this wording fix, that's real evidence this rule_id belongs in STABILIZED_UNCERTAIN_RULE_IDS instead of further prompt tuning — see judge.py.
